=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py: line 316 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The shipped root checker reads active-run statuses in `queued`, `in_progress`, `pending` order instead of lifecycle order, so a run that advances from pending between reads can be missed.
  WHY: The checker can report no active review and hand the PR to a fixer while review is still running; the root/template divergence also fails ordering and parity tests.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/check_in_status.py (and .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py): lines ~388-405 (twin) / ~372-399 (root) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `_complete_dispatch_run_listing` captures `total_count` only from page 1, so a new run inserted at the top during pagination can be omitted while the listing is reported complete.
  WHY: If the omitted run is this PR's active review, the checker can hand the PR to a fixer mid-review.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/check_in_status.py (and .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py): lines ~388-396 (twin) / ~372-380 (root) | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Absent-wrapper detection depends on the literal substring `"HTTP 404"` in `gh api` error text.
  WHY: If `gh` changes its error wording, a missing wrapper can raise `ReadError` instead of being treated as absent, causing retries on hand-backs for consumer repos lacking that wrapper.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml: Line 4416 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The `review / codex-agent` check failed at the reviewer-model step on head `2b3a7946d51097cbf1fa223a544309da40909d61`.
  WHY: The reviewer pipeline did not complete successfully on this PR head, leaving its check failed and the failure unresolved before merge.
- tests/test_check_in_status_hand_back.py: test_incomplete_dispatch_listing_defers_the_hand_back parametrize cases | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The test matrix has no case where `total_count` grows between pages and only a shifted duplicate appears on the later page.
  WHY: The existing cases would not catch the listing-growth bug, allowing it to go undetected.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/check_in_status.py: _complete_dispatch_run_listing module docstring (none present) and module docstring budget block (lines 82-89) | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The operator-visible vocabulary for incomplete-listing errors is not documented or pinned by a contract test.
  WHY: A future edit could remove the reason from an error while preserving the behavior, without the existing test catching the loss of diagnostic detail.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: Statuses are read in lifecycle order (pending, queued, in_progress), so a run that moves forward between two reads is seen by the later read.
  expected_change_site: .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py at line 316 (statuses tuple) and docstring lines 304-321
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py retains the old statuses tuple and lacks the lifecycle-order docstring paragraph; workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/check_in_status.py has the update; tests that load the root copy assert lifecycle order and parity.
- requirement: Each wrapper's listing is read page by page until every run its total_count reports has been read, and a listing that grew under the pagination window must be recognized as incomplete rather than reported complete.
  expected_change_site: workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/check_in_status.py at _complete_dispatch_run_listing lines 388-405 (and the shipped-copy mirror)
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: `_complete_dispatch_run_listing` captures `total_count` only on page 1; the existing tests cover a same-total shift or growth landing on a read page, not growth that pushes a run past the pages read.
- requirement: The §26 hand-back's Incomplete dispatch listing failure mode must report the wrapper, status, and reason in the JSON error field so operators can diagnose a persistent failure.
  expected_change_site: workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/check_in_status.py at _complete_dispatch_run_listing lines 388-405, plus the module docstring's API budget block
  confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The existing test asserts only that "internal-review.yml" appears in `out["error"]`; the module docstring's API budget does not enumerate the reason vocabulary.
- requirement: The shipped `.claude/scripts/check_in_status.py` `_active_run_count` docstring describes the current behavior, including the new helper, per-wrapper/per-status paging, and lifecycle-order invariant.
  expected_change_site: `.claude/scripts/check_in_status.py` lines 304-315 (docstring)
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  EVIDENCE: The shipped copy's `_active_run_count` docstring describes the pre-#5442 behavior and omits the helper, per-wrapper/per-status paging, and lifecycle-order invariant present in the twin.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/check_in_status.py | severity=high | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `_complete_dispatch_run_listing` captures `total_count` from page 1 and reuses it for the break condition and post-loop check; if a new dispatch is inserted at position 1 between page reads, the distinct-ID count can reach the stale count and the listing is returned while omitting the new run.
  WHY: If the missed run is the PR's review dispatch, the checker reports zero active runs, the hand-back fires, and a fixer starts against a live review.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/check_in_status.py and .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The absent-wrapper detection couples to `gh api`'s error wording via the literal substring `HTTP 404`.
  WHY: If `gh` rewords its HTTP error messages, callers report retry for repos lacking one of the wrappers.
- TASK_GAP | Requirement: The statuses are read in lifecycle order (pending, queued, in_progress) in both the shipped and template copies of `_active_run_count`, with a docstring paragraph documenting the lifecycle-order invariant (commit 2b3a794 'read active run statuses in lifecycle order'). | Expected change site: .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py line 293 (statuses tuple) and lines 282-294 (docstring) | Evidence of absence: The PR diff adds the lifecycle-order statuses tuple ('pending', 'queued', 'in_progress') and lifecycle-order docstring paragraph to the twin (workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/check_in_status.py:293) but leaves the shipped root copy (.claude/scripts/check_in_status.py:293) with the pre-fix order ('queued', 'in_progress', 'pending') and its docstring describing the old behaviour. The twin-first interim default (CLAUDE.md 28.C, until 4785) means the fix ships to the twin first and reaches the root only through a [claude-twin-sync] commit. The PR is explicitly parked on that sync, with a hold claim on head 2b3a794. The test files (tests/test_check_in_status.py, tests/test_check_in_status_hand_back.py) load the root copy and assert the new lifecycle order, so the parity tests and test_run_leaving_pending_during_the_reads_is_still_counted fail against the shipped copy. This is a known process blocker, not a code defect: the supervising session owns the sync step, and the project log records Status: BLOCKED, Waiting on: twin sync. | SEVERITY: MAJOR | ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- TASK_GAP | Requirement: Each wrapper's dispatch-run listing is read page by page until every run its total_count reports has been read, and a listing that grew under the pagination window must be recognized as incomplete rather than reported complete (the plan's goal, and the issue-5442 requirement that an incomplete listing must not produce a hand-back). | Expected change site: workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/check_in_status.py at _complete_dispatch_run_listing | Evidence of absence: _complete_dispatch_run_listing captures total_count from page 1 only and uses that captured value for both the loop break condition and post-loop completeness check. A new run inserted at position 1 between page reads pushes existing runs down the listing, the distinct-ID count reaches the stale total_count, and the function returns the listing as complete while omitting the new run. The plan documents only the same-total shift case ('fewer distinct run ids than total_count reports'), not the grown-listing case where a new run is inserted at position 1. The existing test test_listing_with_duplicates_across_pages_is_complete uses total_count growing from 101 to 102 with the extra run on page 2, so it exercises the benign case (growth lands on a read page). The harmful case (growth pushes a run off the read pages) has no test coverage. | SEVERITY: MAJOR | ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
